Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
309 AM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Rinse and repeat..Daily thunderstorm chances continue along with hot 
and humid conditions through the upcoming weekend ahead. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Patchy morning fog, high humidity, hot temperatures, and daily 
thunderstorm chances continue through early next week. 

- 2) A cold front could arrive late next week and into the weekend 
bringing relief from the heat and humidity. 


&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... Patchy morning fog, high humidity, hot 
temperatures, and daily thunderstorm chances continue through early 
next week. 

More of the same when it comes to the forecast Friday into the 
upcoming weekend. Patchy morning fog gives way to high humidity, hot 
temperatures, and late day thunderstorm chances. This is largely due 
in part to blocking high pressure offshore and continued waves of 
upper level energy pivoting through. The nearest front is back 
toward Chicago with little movement eastward in the coming days due 
blocking high pressure offshore. 

For today, expect similar conditions to what we saw Thursday 
although the severe threat will be higher. A dry and muggy start 
with some fog giving way to mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies in 
the afternoon. The combination of the heat and humidity with boost 
surface based CAPE values above 2000 j/kg+ with DCAPE values 
remaining around or less than 1000 j/kg. 0-6 km shear values will 
sit between 25-30 kts with mid level lapse rates between 6-7.5 C/km 
which would allow for higher storm coverage and more progressive 
movement from west to east across the region. Storms will initiate 
in the lee of the Alleghenies around 18-20z/2-4pm before advancing 
eastward toward the metros toward the late afternoon and evening 
rush hours commute 21-00z/5-8pm as the impulse works through. Storms 
could fire ahead of the shortwave via the bay/river breeze similar 
to what we had on Thursday. With all that saId, SPC has upgraded the 
areas near and along the I-95 (DC/NORTHERN VA burbs northeast 
into central MD) into a Slight Risk (Level 2 out of 5) for 
severe weather this afternoon and evening. The main threats with
storms look to be damaging winds (15% probabilities) and heavy 
rainfall although isolated large hail cannot be ruled out due to
the higher mid-level lapse rates. 

Similar conditions are expected Saturday as another potent shortwave 
passes through. Instability will remain high as a result of the high 
heat and humidity. Shear values will sit around 30 kts perhaps 
increasing to 35 kts as the subtropical jet stream begins to 
strengthen. This could yield a more organized severe weather threat 
with aligns with current learning machine guidance which suggest 15-
30 percent probabilities for damaging wind gusts Saturday afternoon 
and evening. With that said, guidance continues to focus on areas 
along and north of I-66/US-50 for both Friday and Saturday. 

Convection begins to wane a bit Sunday into Monday given quasi-zonal 
flow aloft. It will be short-lived with storm chances increasing 
once again Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday as a series of shortwave 
disturbances passing through. By Wednesday and Thursday, a front 
tries to drop into the region potentially bringing a change to the 
current pattern. 

Outside of the storm chances expect highs in the upper 80s and low 
90s with heat indices east of the BLue Ridge up around 100 degrees. 
The hottest days look to be Sunday through Tuesday given the 
strengthened subtropical ridge over the region.

KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front could arrive late next week and into 
the weekend bringing relief from the heat and humidity.  

While this is very far out in the forecast period, there is some 
signal that a more potent frontal system could push through the 
region late in the week. The details are murky at this stage of the 
forecast, with timing very uncertain, as well as potential impacts. 
Deterministic and ensemble guidance is generally between 
Thursday/Friday right now, with improvement in the weather pattern 
possible into the upcoming weekend. Any decent frontal passage in 
the summertime should be watched closely for potential severe 
weather, so we will keep monitoring this in the coming days to see 
if that potential is there, and try to narrow down the timeframe a 
bit more.


&&

.AVIATION /07Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected across the terminals 
through the middle of next week given subtropical high pressure 
offshore and the lack of any real front passing through. Brief 
periods of sub-VFR are likely during the afternoon and evening 
hours due to thunderstorms. For Friday, expected storms to fire 
west of MRB between 17-19z/1-3pm before advancing eastward into 
the corridor (IAD-BWI-DCA) between 20-01z/4-9pm. PROB30s will be
used to encompass this threat given the coverage being widely 
scattered across the region. A similar set up is expected 
Saturday afternoon and evening with less coverage Sunday. 
Outside of the thunderstorms expect patchy fog between the 
terminals each morning through early next week. Winds will 
remain light out of the south and southeast at less than 15 kts.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories may be needed for portions of the waters 
through Saturday due to southerly channeling mainly in the afternoon 
and evening. Most days will see marginal conditions just below the 
threshold, especially over the open waters. Daily shower and 
thunderstorm chances are expected each afternoon and evening through 
early next week. The greatest coverage will be on Friday and 
Saturday afternoon/evening. Special Marine Warnings may be needed to 
encompass any any stronger thunderstorms that may form. Storms will 
capable of producing frequent lightning and wind gusts over 35
knots.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies climb through the weekend in response to return 
southerly flow. Periods of coastal flooding are possible at times of 
high tide at sensitive locations.
